question: Name two optional pavement-marking features explicitly labeled in Figure 3D-1 at the roundabout.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 3D-1 explicitly labels at least two optional pavement-marking features: (1) optional white diagonal markings placed within the circulatory roadway area adjacent to the splitter islands, and (2) the yellow edge line around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway, which is labeled "Optional" in the figure. Options (permitted): - "A yellow edge line may be placed around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway (see Figure 3D-1) and may be used to channelize traffic." - "Channelizing lines (see Section 3B.08) and chevron and diagonal markings (see Section 3B.25) may be used on the approaches to and within the circulatory roadway of multi-lane roundabouts to separate traffic lanes, discourage lane changing, and/or compensate for off-tracking of larger trucks and vehicles." - "YIELD (word) (see Figure 3D-1) and YIELD AHEAD (symbol or word) pavement markings may be used on approaches to roundabouts." Guidance (recommended): - Where a white edge line is used for the circulatory roadway, it should be: "A. A solid line adjacent to the splitter island, and B. A wide dotted line across the lane(s) entering the roundabout" (see Figure 3D-1). Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 3D-1 shows a callout reading "Optional white diagonal markings" pointing to the white hatched area near the east splitter island, and an "Optional" callout with a leader line pointing to the yellow edge line around the inner edge of the circulatory roadway. [Image 2] The full-page view of Figure 3D-1 (page 596) confirms these same labels, including the "Optional" callouts, the "Optional white diagonal markings" label, and the "Wide dotted white extension of circulatory roadway edge line" annotation. [Image 4] Figure 3D-3 (Sheet 1) similarly labels "Optional white diagonal markings" with an asterisk legend for "Optional," consistent with Figure 3D-1's treatment. [Image 5] Figure 3D-3 (Sheet 2, Drawing B) shows the "Optional yellow edge line and diagonal yellow markings," which corresponds to the channelizing use of the yellow inner edge line referenced from Figure 3D-1. [Image 3] Figure 3D-8 shows additional optional markings (white chevron and diagonal yellow markings) at roundabout ramp terminals, illustrating the same optional treatments in another context. Citations: - Section 3D.03 Option §4 (p.605) - Section 3D.02 Option §5 (p.595) - Section 3D.05 Option §1 (p.605) - Section 3D.03 Guidance §2 (p.595) - Section 3D.01 Support §4 (p.595) - Figure 3D-1 (p.596) - Page 637 - Page 639 - Page 640
